body.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), use leave-one-cell-out residuals only on \(\mathcal V_n\), while keeping the covariance sum on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). The resulting unit-heteroskedastic plug-in estimator satisfies \[\max_{k,k'\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|/(s_ks_{k'})=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2}),\qquad \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|\widehat s_k/s_k-1|=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-1}).\] In particular, \(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) while retaining every shared treated-, donor-, and pre-treatment-cell product.
body.justification: The multiplier law is usable only if its entire growing covariance matrix, not only each diagonal entry, is estimable under bounded unit heteroskedasticity.
body.gap: The accessible Choi--Yuan article points to Supplement G.2 but does not substantiate a horizon-uniform covariance theorem; Choi--Kwon--Liao's Feasible CLT displays unitwise residual variance only for a fixed group-average functional, and Ben-Michael--Feller leave staggered heteroskedastic inference as a last-mile task.
body.consumer: This gives the feasible covariance input for one studentized whole-curve critical value in a state-policy panel.

obligation.what_is_open: A primitive uniform rate for the joint estimation error of the feasible event-by-cell score loadings, including both \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) and the leave-one-cell-out unit-variance errors.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen replication condition controls only the number of untreated variance-training cells.  No assumption or established result bounds the leave-one-cell-out imputation error or the estimated Choi--Yuan loading coefficients in the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) norm at the required \(o_P((\log(2K))^{-2})\) rate.  Assuming that score-loading rate would assume the theorem's substantive crux.
obligation.attempted: Decomposed the normalized covariance error into two score-loading errors and derived a sharp deterministic Cauchy--Schwarz bound.  Tried to obtain the missing rate from variance replication and the unscaled signal, spectral, and block envelopes, but those premises contain no result transporting their rates to \(\widehat c\) or cross-fitted residuals with the required powers of \(\log(2K)\).
obligation.partial_result:
The missing stochastic assertion can be isolated by a deterministic
calculation.  Under row heteroskedasticity define
\[
\widehat b_{kq}
=\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
a_{kq}=\frac{c_{kq}\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad q=(u,v),
\]
and put
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
(\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The definition of \(s_k\) gives \(\sum_q a_{kq}^2=1\).  Therefore,
by adding and subtracting the two cross terms and applying
Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}
&=\left|\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q}
-\sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}\right|\\
&\le
\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2\|a_{k'}\|_2
+\|a_k\|_2\|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2
+\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2
 \|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\le 2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the first claimed covariance rate would follow from the primitive
score-loading conclusion
\(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\), uniformly over the
slice.  The diagonal case and
\(\lvert\sqrt{1+x}-1\rvert\le\lvert x\rvert\) for \(x>-1\) then give
the stated standard-error rate (in fact the stronger
\(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) rate), and division by the two consistently
estimated diagonal scales gives
\(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\).
The frozen assumptions do not establish the displayed
\(\ell_2\)-score-loading conclusion: variance replication controls the
sampling fluctuation of true residual squares, but no frozen result
controls the leave-one-cell-out imputation errors and estimated
Choi--Yuan loading coefficients at this logarithmic rate.
